title: A Scholarship for the Group Chat
premise: Oscar Okafor has spent senior year being nobody: the invisible eldest sibling who cooks dinner, checks homework, and keeps his head down while his mom works nights. When his best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only her car keys and a half-deleted group chat, Oscar discovers she was investigating the scholarship fund that was supposed to be his lifeline—and someone powerful made her disappear. With his little sister Zuri's hacking skills and a reluctant ally in the school's golden boy, Oscar uncovers a corruption ring run by the very people deciding who gets to escape their neighborhood. In the end, Oscar must choose between accepting a hushed-up settlement that secures his future or exposing everything at the championship game, where he chooses justice over the scholarship—finding that the community he stopped hiding from becomes the family that catches him.
about_author: Gideon Amberdale is a former night-shift paramedic who wrote his first novel in hospital break rooms, fueled by vending machine coffee and the stories teenagers tell when adults stop listening. He lives in Ohio with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy attachment to high school basketball.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A day-in-the-life establishing chapter: Oscar microwaves dinner for his siblings, aces a chemistry quiz, and dodges a guidance counselor asking about college applications. The emotional beat is quiet exhaustion—the cost of invisibility shown as love, not weakness.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Priya misses their standing study session, then doesn't answer texts. The group chat fills with jokes that curdle into worry. At midnight, her last message appears: 'check the fund.' Emotional beat: dread arriving in small, deniable increments.

chapters.title: Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Police call it a runaway; Priya's mom knows better. On Priya's porch, Oscar finds her car keys in an envelope with his name on them—a message meant only for him. Beat: guilt ignites; he was her best friend and missed every sign.

chapters.title: Zuri Breaks the Password
chapters.summary: Alternating Oscar/Zuri POV. Oscar finally lets little sister Zuri into the secret; she cracks Priya's cloud backup and finds screenshots of the Whitfield Scholarship Fund's books—numbers that don't add up. Beat: the family becomes a team, and hiding stops being an option.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signs the Checks
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar interviews for the scholarship with Dr. Harlan Voss, school board treasurer, whose warmth feels rehearsed. Voss mentions Priya unprompted: 'Such a troubled girl.' Beat: first direct contact with the antagonist; fear dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Golden Boy, Tarnished
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. Star athlete Deacon Reyes—Voss's protégé—catches Oscar photographing fund documents. Instead of reporting him, Deacon admits he found something similar before the season started and stayed silent. Beat: uneasy alliance forged in mutual shame.

chapters.title: What Priya Found
chapters.summary: Zuri's POV. Decrypted files reveal Voss skimmed scholarship money for years, and Priya had contacted a journalist. Her final draft email names a second accomplice inside the school. Beat: the mystery sharpens from 'where is she' to 'who helped make her disappear.'

chapters.title: Mom Works Nights
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Mom comes home early, sensing something wrong; Oscar almost tells her, then can't—she'd make him quit, and quitting means Priya stays lost. Beat: the theme of duty versus truth crystallizes within the family itself.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Maple Street
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. Someone follows Oscar home. Deacon runs interference, and they realize Voss knows what they know. Beat: stakes turn physical; the investigation now endangers the siblings Oscar swore to protect.

chapters.title: The Empty Storage Unit
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following Priya's keys—one opens a storage facility—they find her unit emptied except for a burner phone with one saved voicemail: Voss threatening her. Beat: proof at last, but also confirmation of how dangerous Voss is.

chapters.title: Midseason
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. The championship run continues as distraction and cover; Deacon plays brilliantly while dying inside about his silence. Coach pressures him about 'loyalty.' Beat: power's corruption shown through sport—winning as complicity.

chapters.title: Runaway, They Said
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Police close Priya's case as voluntary. Her mother sobs on Oscar's shoulder; Oscar realizes the system won't save anyone here. Beat: grief converts to resolve—justice outside the law becomes the only path.

chapters.title: The Accomplice Wears a Lanyard
chapters.summary: Zuri's POV. Zuri identifies the insider: Vice Principal Marsh, who falsified Priya's attendance records to support the runaway story. They confront her; she cracks, admitting Voss paid her but claims she never touched Priya. Beat: first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Offer Letter
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Voss offers Oscar the full ride plus cash 'for family expenses'—contingent on returning Priya's keys and forgetting her name. Beat: temptation made explicit; the corruption offers Oscar exactly what his family needs.

chapters.title: Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. Deacon publicly quits the booster club fundraiser, burning his own scholarship prospects, and tells Oscar why: 'I watched you choose your sister over yourself every single day.' Beat: Deacon's redemption; friendship becomes love against duty.

chapters.title: Where She Went
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following the burner phone's pings, they find Priya alive—hiding with her aunt two states away, terrified after Voss ran her off the road. Beat: relief and fury entwined; the missing person chooses to come back and testify.

chapters.title: The Journalist Returns the Call
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (first appearance). Priya, Oscar, and Zuri compile evidence for reporter Dana Okafor-Hughes—no relation, which Priya calls fate. But the story needs one irrefutable document still locked in Voss's office. Beat: the plan forms around the championship game.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar tells Mom everything. Instead of forbidding him, she hands him her late father's camera bag for smuggling documents and says, 'We do this together.' Beat: the family secret dissolves into family strength; quiet before the storm.

chapters.title: Championship Night
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. While Deacon plays the game of his life, Oscar and Zuri slip into Voss's office during the packed gymnasium. Alarm trips; Voss confronts them mid-heist. Beat: climax begins—caught red-handed, both literally and morally.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Voss offers Oscar everything one final time, alone, no witnesses. Oscar records the confession on Priya's phone and walks out past the cheering crowd as the buzzer sounds. Beat: climax resolved—justice chosen over the scholarship, labels fully off.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Voss and Marsh are arrested; the story breaks statewide. The scholarship fund is frozen, meaning Oscar loses the money—but a community-funded replacement emerges, and Priya returns to finish senior year beside him. Beat: consequences honored, losses real.

chapters.title: Keys to Everything
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Graduation-adjacent epilogue: Oscar returns Priya's keys, accepts a smaller state-school offer, and watches Zuri get recognized for her role in the investigation. Final beat: visibility chosen freely—the boy who hid learns he was never invisible to the people who mattered.
